name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area Q3 GDP rose 0.4% and October composite PMI slipped to 51.7, both still above the Normal lines
state: Euro-area GDP rose 0.4% in Q3 on Eurostat's flash estimate of 30 Oct, after 0.6% in Q2 (Eurostat via Hellenic Shipping News). The final October composite PMI, released on 4 Nov, was 51.7, down from 53.1 in September (Teleborsa via Borsa Italiana). Inflation rose to 4.0% in October from 3.8% as energy costs climbed (Eurostat via Tradingsat). Growth is slowing, but both measures remain on the Normal side as of 8 Nov.
for_you: Slower growth and higher energy costs fall hardest on energy-intensive firms and on households with large energy bills. Exporters to the euro area are exposed if demand weakens further.
rubric_hit: Positive GDP (+0.4% Q3) and composite PMI 51.7 above 50: Normal line

sources.title: Hellenic Shipping News — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
Borsa Italiana — Unione Europea, PMI composito in ottobre
Tradingsat — Zone euro: l'inflation annuelle atteint 4% en octobre

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
